question: In many traditional Nigerian communities, how was maternal and child health viewed regarding fathers?

options.A: It was managed entirely by traditional birth attendants.
options.B: It was considered the primary duty of the local chief.
options.C: It was the direct responsibility of the federal health ministry.
options.D: It was viewed strictly as a female domain.

explanation: Historically, pregnancy and childcare spaces were culturally set aside for women only, which kept men out of the process. You're doing great!

question: Why is modern healthcare now encouraging fathers to get involved during pregnancy?

options.A: Government policies now fine fathers who stay away.
options.B: Women are no longer able to attend clinics alone.
options.C: Shared decision-making improves overall health outcomes.
options.D: Hospitals have extra space to accommodate couples.

explanation: When men are involved, health choices and money are planned together, leading to a healthier family! Keep it up.

question: What is a major clinical benefit when a husband knows basic pregnancy danger signs?

options.A: He can arrange timely transport during an emergency.
options.B: He can diagnose malaria without laboratory tests.
options.C: He can safely perform a delivery at home if needed.
options.D: He can prescribe iron supplements to his wife.

explanation: Spotting danger signs early means partners can act fast and avoid deadly delays in reaching the hospital. Brilliant!

question: Why do mothers with involved partners tend to have better clinic attendance?

options.A: Hospitals give financial rewards to couples who attend together.
options.B: Mothers refuse to leave the house without a male escort.
options.C: Shared responsibility reduces maternal stress and logistical hurdles.
options.D: Fathers force their wives to visit the doctor daily.

explanation: When partners share the load, going to appointments becomes much easier and less stressful for the mother.

question: Which of these is a major barrier that keeps Nigerian men away from maternal clinics?

options.A: Traditional beliefs that babies bring bad luck
options.B: Long waiting times that conflict with daily work
options.C: Federal laws forbidding men from entering wards
options.D: A complete lack of roads leading to any hospital

explanation: Since many men hustle for daily wages, spending hours waiting at a clinic can hurt their daily survival. Makes total sense!

question: How do negative staff attitudes in hospitals affect male involvement?

options.A: They motivate men to build private clinics.
options.B: They discourage men from returning to the clinic.
options.C: They have no real effect on attendance rates.
options.D: They force men to study nursing on their own.

explanation: When nurses act unfriendly or unwelcoming, men feel unwanted and prefer to stay away next time.

question: In a patriarchal family setup, who typically makes the final financial and health decisions?

options.A: The youngest child in the family
options.C: The male head of the household

explanation: In patriarchal settings, financial and key decision-making power usually rests with the male head. You've got this!

question: Why can traditional power dynamics sometimes delay medical care for pregnant women?

options.A: Women are legally banned from talking to doctors first.
options.B: Hospitals refuse to treat women without a signed consent form.
options.C: Men always prefer traditional herbs over modern medicine.
options.D: The woman may need to wait for the man's approval and funds.

explanation: When getting care depends entirely on someone else's permission and money, emergencies can worsen while waiting.

question: What is a great way for a father to support the mother after childbirth?

options.A: Isolating the newborn from all family members
options.B: Taking over exclusive breastfeeding duties from the mother
options.C: Assisting with household chores to help the mother rest
options.D: Refusing to allow visitors into the family compound

explanation: New mothers need plenty of physical rest to recover, so a partner stepping in with chores is a huge help!

question: A husband accompanies his pregnant wife to antenatal care. What should the nurse encourage him to learn?

options.A: Counsel other couples in the waiting room.
options.B: Learn about pregnancy danger signs and birth preparedness.
options.C: Perform a physical abdominal examination on his wife.
options.D: Prescribe prenatal vitamins to prevent anemia.

explanation: Teaching partners about warning signs ensures they can act quickly if an emergency happens. Wonderful!

question: How can a father directly support good child nutrition at home?

options.A: By mixing infant formula with fresh cow milk
options.B: By providing funds for diverse and nutritious food items
options.C: By growing all the household crops by himself
options.D: By deciding the exact feeding times for the mother

explanation: Providing money to buy quality, healthy food is one of the best ways fathers contribute to child nutrition.

question: Why is it helpful for fathers to attend child growth monitoring sessions?

options.A: They must record the child's weight in the main register.
options.B: They can help spot early signs of malnutrition.
options.C: They are required to administer the routine vaccines.
options.D: They prevent the mother from asking questions.

explanation: Growth charts let fathers clearly see how their child is developing and catch nutrition issues early.

question: What practical change can nurses advocate for to help more men attend clinics?

options.A: Charging male visitors a special facility fee
options.B: Scheduling weekend or evening clinic hours
options.C: Requiring fathers to wear special uniforms
options.D: Banning all female relatives from the waiting room

explanation: Flexible clinic hours make it possible for men who work during regular weekdays to attend.

question: A nurse notices male partners sitting in the antenatal waiting room look ignored and uncomfortable. What should she do?

options.A: Tell the pregnant women to handle their husbands at home.
options.B: Ask security guards to escort them outside.
options.C: Greet them warmly and include them in the health talk.
options.D: Ignore them since antenatal care is only for women.

explanation: Welcoming men and including them in discussions builds trust and makes them want to return. Great nursing care!

question: Which key community figures can nurses partner with to encourage male involvement?
explanation: Traditional and religious leaders command great respect and can easily help shift community attitudes toward male participation.

question: Why are community-based approaches important alongside clinic visits?

options.A: They allow nurses to fine men who refuse to visit the clinic.
options.B: They replace the need for any hospitals or clinics in rural areas.
options.C: They reach men within their own social environments and cultural comfort zones.
options.D: They ensure that women stay indoors during pregnancy.

explanation: Taking health talks to town halls and local spots engages men right where they naturally gather. Fantastic job!
